question:
A 53-year-old male presents to the emergency department with a three-day history of copious watery
diarrhea, nausea, and weakness, accompanied by a two-day history of not eating. His medical history
includes gastroesophageal reflux disease and a recent dental infection. His medications include
famotidine, omeprazole, and he recently completed a 10-day course of clindamycin. Physical
examination reveals a temperature of 39.3 ºC (102.7 ºF), heart rate of 120/min, respiratory rate of
28/min, and SpO2 of 99% on room air. Despite receiving 2 liters of 0.9% sodium chloride, his blood
pressure remains at 78/41 mmHg. Abdominal examination shows rigidity with hypoactive bowel
sounds. Laboratory results indicate a white blood cell count of 28,000/mL, creatinine of 2.6 mg/dL, and
lactic acid of 3.8 mmol/L. What is the most appropriate next step in managing this patient? Answer
Choices: (A) Administer intravenous metronidazole (B) Obtain stool culture and sensitivity (C) Begin
oral vancomycin and metronidazole combination therapy (D) Administer oral metronidazole (E) Repeat
lactic acid level (F) Start intravenous vancomycin (G) Computed tomography of abdomen (H) Perform
flexible sigmoidoscopy (I) Initiate droplet precautions (J) Initiate total parenteral nutrition
 A. Initiate droplet precautions
B. Begin oral vancomycin and metronidazole combination therapy
C. Initiate total parenteral nutrition
D. Perform flexible sigmoidoscopy
E. Computed tomography of abdomen
F. Repeat lactic acid level
G. Start intravenous vancomycin
H. Obtain stool culture and sensitivity

I. Administer intravenous metronidazole
J. Administer oral metronidazole
